html:
Ali Hujwiri was a Persian Sufi scholar from Ghazni, in today's Afghanistan, who settled in Lahore in the 11th century and is buried there. He is known as Data Ganj Bakhsh, the giver of treasures.

He came to Lahore when it was held by the Ghaznavids, the dynasty of Mahmud of Ghazni. There he wrote the Kashf al-Mahjub, the Unveiling of the Veiled, the oldest treatise on Sufism in Persian. It explains the Sufi path and defends it as part of orthodox Islam.

His shrine, Data Darbar, is the largest in South Asia and draws crowds day and night, with free food for the poor. Later saints of the Chishti order are said to have paid homage there before going on to India. In 2010 suicide bombers attacked the shrine, killing dozens of people.
